newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Opposition leader Chuan Leekpai has warned against any attempt to incite public unrest if the new constitution does not come up to expectations. He says public figures should refrain from even suggesting the likelihood of bloodshed should the new constitution prove unpopular. (THE NATION)

- The prime minister wants three highly profitable state enterprises to be privatised in a bid to boost foreign investment. The enterprises in question are the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand, the Telephone Organisation of Thailand and the Communications Authority of Thailand. The privatisation is expected to be implemened next year. The move is designed to curb the serious current account deficit that has continued to pound economic growth. (BANGKOK POST)

- The government will reveal the identities of politicians and officials with links to the drug trade after the New Year holiday, at the same time the Police Department moves against officers believed to be involved in trafficking. An official admits that legal action cannot be taken against most of the suspects. (THE NATION)

- Incoming director of the Excise Department Somchai Richuphan sees the restructuring of the tax system as one of his most urgent tasks. He will work on the changes once he takes up the post on January 6. He says a selection system will categorise which goods should be classed as luxury items and subject to a high excise tax rate. (BANGKOK POST)

- The automotive industry is set to be transformed next year from mainly domestic consumption to an export-oriented industry, as exports are likely to reach 20,000 vehicles, or double the figure of 10,000 expected for this year. The Federation of Thai Industries forecasts exports will gradually climb to 100,000 units in 1999, once the 135,000-vehicle capacity joint assembly plant of Ford and Mazda and the 100,000-unit capacity plant of General Motors are operational. (BUSINESS DAY)
